reasons: Aggregation differs: the Datadog query is sum:redis.net.clients, but the candidate uses avg(). Over multiple series, avg divides the total by the series count, so the value is wrong.

Series set differs: the Datadog query filters on $host (prefix host, default *), which should become a host=~"$host" matcher. The candidate drops it, so it covers all hosts regardless of the selected host.

Quantity and unit match: redis.clients.connected (unit {client}, non-monotonic sum) measures the same connected-client count as redis.net.clients, and the candidate correctly does not apply rate() to a non-monotonic sum.

The $host matcher needs a label for the host. The dataset lists only redis_version as observed, so the host label name cannot be confirmed from the dataset; the converter should check this before emitting the matcher.

Outcome translated is acceptable because an exact mapping exists. The correct expression would be sum({otel_metric_name="redis.clients.connected", otel_metric_type="sum", <host label>=~"$host"}), with the $scope variable dropped since it has no prefix.
